handDesc.handNote: Main text and any darker interventions are distinguished where observed. No individual historical correcting hands are inferred from tonal contrast in monochrome photographs.

origin.p: The supplied BnF IIIF manifest dates the manuscript to 1001–1100. The catalogue dating is not a date assigned to individual interventions.

surrogates.p: The original full-resolution digital images and enlarged crops were inspected for this first pass. Gallica source reuse conditions apply. No text was populated from LL or another witness.

projectDesc.p: All48 extant verse positions and every first-reader note were independently checked by a different agent against the actual source images. Original annotation rectangles are unchanged. Manuscript spellings, local uncertainty and source insets are retained without importing another witness’s text.

correction.p: No silent emendation from an edition or another witness. Local uncertain letters use unclear, irrecoverable text or signs use gap. Observed above-line letters use add. Tonal distinctions use hi without an invented underlying erased text or historical hand. Manuscript annotations use note type manuscript, distinct from editorial evidence notes.

normalization.p: One source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs, long s, and capitals are represented in legible Latin types. Word boundaries are editorially segmented; no indentation whitespace is inserted inside verse mixed content. Selected ligatures and abbreviation signs are declared typographic approximations; explicit expansions remain in TEI rather than a separate reading mode. This is not a facsimile-perfect inventory of every minute stroke.

punctuation.p: Significant observed punctuation is retained schematically, without adding systematic modern sentence punctuation.

segmentation.p: Each l represents a verse and physical written line at its canonical poem position. Elegiac couplets are editorial grouping. Indentation is encoded only where the inspected source layout supports an offset; it is not inferred automatically from verse parity. Page breaks follow the photographed left/right physical pages. Facsimile zones reproduce the existing annotation rectangles unchanged; they may include neighbouring ink and exclude marginal annotations.

interpretation.p: First-pass evidence notes are a working queue for an independent agent, not assignments for the human editor. Genuine source uncertainty remains local; consequential unresolved interpretation is distinguished from ordinary observation.

revisionDesc.change: Completed first reading from source images and enlarged crops, with line coverage and evidence notes. Independent second reading not yet performed.
Independently inspected all48 source verses and27 original notes; corrected readings, abbreviation form and source sign, retained unresolved local fading, and confirmed full-page indentation.

lg.l: Annua uenerunt cerealis tempora sacri
Secubat in uacuo sola puella toro
Flaua ceres tenues spicis redimita capillos
Cur inhibes sacris commoda nostra tuis
Te dea munificam gentes ubique loquuntur
Nec minus humanis inuidet illa bonis
Ante nec hirsutis ornabat farra colonis
Nec notum terris area nomen erat
Glandiferas quercus oracula prima ferebant
Hoc erat &et teneri cespitis herba cibus
Prima ceres docuit turgescere semen in agris
Falce coloratas subsecuitque comas
Prima iugis tauros supponere colla coegit
Et ueterem curuo dente reuellit humum
Hanc quisquam lacrimis &et tristitia
Et bene tormentis secubituque coli
Nec tamen est quāquamuis agros amet illa feraces
Rustica nec uiduum pectus amoris habet
Cretes erunt testes nec fingunt omnes cretes
Crete nutrito terra superba ioui
Illic sideream mundi qui temperat arcem
Exiguus tenero lac bibit ore puer
Magna fides testi testis laudatur alumno
Fassuram cererem crimina nostra puto
Viderat iasium cretea diua sub ida
Figentem certa terga ferina manu
Vidit &et ut tenere flammam rapuere medulle
Hinc pudor ex illa parte trahebat amor
Victus amore pudor sulcos ardere uideres
Et sata cum minima parte redire sui
Cum bene iactatos pulsarant arua ligones
Ruperat &et duram uomer aduncus humum
Seminaque in latos ierant equaliter agros
Irrita decepti uota colentis erant
Diua potens frugum siluis cessabat in altis
Deciderant longe spicea serta come
Sola crete fecundo fertilisc anno
Omnia qua tulerat se dea messis erat
Ipse locus nemorum canebat frugibus ide
Et ferus in silua farra metebat aper
Optauit minos similes sibi legifer annos

l.unclear: Optasset cereris longus ut esset amor

lg.l: QoQuod tibi secubitus tristes dea flaua fuissent
Hoc cogor sacris nunc ego ferre tuis
Cur ego sim tristis cum sit tibi nata reperta
Regnaque quam iuno sorte minore regat
Festa dies ueneremque uocat cantusque merumque
Hec decet ad dominos munera ferre deos

div.head: Reviewed transcription notes
div.note: Independent full-opening and verse inspection confirms Annua uenerunt and Secubat as this poem’s first couplet, not a heading. The flourished A spans its opening area. All48 extant verses are present; full images95 and96 support the modest alternating insets recorded in the XML.

The source supports Flaua ceres tenues spicis redimita capillos. Small darker marks near and below the end of redimita remain documented as visible marks; their function and any earlier deleted letter are not established. No historical hand is inferred.

The marked and crowded group after Te dea remains tentatively munificam. Enlargements do not securely separate all its minims or establish the function of the small adjacent marks. Gentes ubique loquuntur is supported; the uncertainty stays local.
The enlarged line supports Ante nec hirsutis ornabat farra colonis. These source endings and the written verb are retained without substituting a different edition’s wording.
The faint minim sequence after Nec remains tentatively notum. Terris area nomen erat is supported. Enlarging the source does not justify removing the local uncertainty.

The source has a protruding G followed by a faint sequence provisionally landiferas. Its complete spelling remains uncertain. Quercus oracula prima ferebant is supported; the source does not justify replacing the pale opening with a familiar phrase.
The source supports Hoc erat, the et ligature and teneri cespitis herba cibus. The glyph and explicit expansion retain the visible sign; Hoc and cespitis are not normalized.

The faint opening shows an ascender and alce-like sequence, tentatively Falce, rather than the first-pass Prima. The corrected opening remains locally unclear because of fading. Coloratas subsecuitque comas is supported.

The bottom-left verse remains faded, with iugis and supponere colla coegit provisional. Prima and tauros are more legible. The entire source position survives; no missing letters are supplied from another witness.
The faint central phrase ueterem curuo dente remains locally unclear. The initial Et and final reuellit humum are supported. Fading alone is not encoded as an erasure.

The first right-page verse supports Hanc quisquam lacrimis and the et sign. The subsequent tentative tristitia and illegible ending remain conservative: the photograph does not establish a complete phrase. The gap describes illegible ink within this surviving verse, not source absence.
A visible nasal bar marks quā before the written uis, supporting the separate quam expansion. Nec tamen est and agros amet illa feraces agree with the source.
Both cretes forms are visible. After fingunt the source reads omnes, including the final s, correcting first-pass omnia. The next verse begins Crete and ends ioui; these source forms are retained.
Magna fides testi testis laudatur alumno is visible, including the repeated testi testis. No second word is removed or supplied.
The name after Viderat remains tentatively iasium because its pale initial strokes cannot all be securely separated. Cretea diua sub ida is supported in the manuscript’s spelling.
The source supports the et sign, ut tenere flammam rapuere medulle. The plain-e endings remain as written; nearby mottling does not establish a recoverable cancellation.
The source supports Hinc pudor ex illa parte trahebat amor. The following verse visibly reads ardere, retained without normalization.
Cum bene iactatos is supported; the marked and mottled verb remains tentatively pulsarant. Arua ligones is legible. The uncertain verb is not expanded or replaced from another witness.
The source reads duram, with the a before m visible, correcting first-pass durum. Ruperat, the et sign, uomer aduncus humum agree with the source.
The pale opening Irrita decepti remains tentative. Uota colentis erant is supported. The local uncertainty is retained after enlargement.
The source supports Deciderant longe spicea serta come. Plain-e forms remain as written, and the source initial follows the observed modest inset.

The pale opening remains tentatively Sola crete; no omitted expected word is asserted. Fertilis also remains uncertain. The separate darker high sign is c-like rather than the first-pass t-like form, now represented as tentative c. Its relation to the baseline and the nearby point is unresolved; no substitution sequence is invented.
The complete source verse supports Omnia qua tulerat se dea messis erat. No normalized spelling or alternate wording is supplied.

The final letter of the opening is pale and e-like, represented as Ips with a tentative e rather than the first-pass definite Ipsa. Locus nemorum canebat frugibus ide is supported. The uncertain letter is kept local.

The opening remains tentatively Optauit. The enlarged later sequence visibly reads legifer annos, including the tall f, correcting the first-pass legis in annos. Minos similes sibi is supported. Only the unresolved opening remains unclear.

The final right-page line is very faded. Its tentative Optasset cereris longus ut esset amor remains wholly qualified; the photograph does not establish all its letters securely. No stronger reading is supplied from a different witness.

The opening is a large Q with a separate high o-like sign, now encoded as a source abbreviation with qualified Quod expansion rather than four conjectured baseline letters. Tibi secubitus tristes dea flaua fuissent is supported. The raised sign itself remains locally unclear.

The enlarged source supports sacris nunc and the ending ferre tuis. The faint opening is now provisionally Hoc cogor and the short group after nunc provisionally ego, both locally unclear. This corrects the unsupported first-pass segmentation Hoc ego cur and ending cogor inesse; no full certainty is claimed for the pale words.

Hec decet ad dominos munera ferre deos is visible. The following large M and separate marginal annotation belong to the next poem. All48 positions and the final boundary were checked; original rectangles are unchanged.
